titlePlain: A Cluster Outage From a Missing
subtitle: Lesson 31 · Capstone: Running a Real Application on Kubernetes (illustrative scenario)

containers:

caption: Copied from an older manifest and trimmed down -- nobody noticed the resources block never made it in.

code:
kubectl get pods -o wide

NAME                    STATUS       NODE
order-worker-7f8d9c7b6   OOMKilled    node-3
nightly-report-28891234  Error        node-3
order-api-5c9b8f7d4       Evicted      node-3
caption: Two correctly-configured pods failed on the same node as the one pod with no memory ceiling.

steps.label: OOMKilled
steps.sub: The kernel's OOMKiller kills a specific process once memory truly runs out

steps.label: Evicted
steps.sub: The kubelet proactively removes a pod to relieve node-wide pressure, earlier

steps.label: Neither pod did anything wrong
steps.sub: Both were healthy, correctly-configured, and caught in a neighbor's blast radius

caption: A LimitRange gives the next forgotten resources block a safe default automatically, on admission.

subtitle: Reviewing all eight chapters through the lens of this one incident and this one app.
